status.main_product: Agricultural drones, drone training, and Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS)
status.scope_reason: The company itself manufactures agricultural drones and provides drone training and Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) for the precision agriculture industry.
status.evidence: In January 2025, DroneAcharya Aerial Innovations signed a term sheet for a strategic merger with AVPL International, which provides drone manufacturing, training, and Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) from its headquarters in Gurugram, India.

claims.claim: The company reports its DGCA type-certified agricultural flagship model, the "VIRAJ" drone, is a twin battery-powered system featuring both a 10-litre tank for chemical spraying and a 10-litre seed dispenser for seed broadcasting applications.

The company reports it offers the Viraj 1.0 and Viraj 2.0 variants for precision spraying, seed broadcasting, and crop inspection, alongside separate announcements for high-capacity 30-litre crop-protection spraying models and a 5 kg payload logistics drop drone.
The company reports that its Viraj 2.0 agriculture drone features a 10-litre spraying capacity and utilizes a centrifugal nozzle for precision spraying to provide uniform coverage and reduce waste.
The company reports that it offers a high-capacity 30-litre Kisan drone designed for large-scale precision spraying applications to ensure uniform coverage across fields.
claims.note: The name "Kisan drone" could not be verified in connection with AVPL's high-capacity 30-litre model, which is typically branded under the "Viraj" series (Viraj 30/40L).

claims.claim: In its draft red herring prospectus, the company notes that its technical capabilities include integration of components such as LiDAR payloads based on customer requirement specifications.
claims.source: AITMC Ventures Limited (AVPL International) Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus (UDRHP) filed with BSE/NSE (https://www.bseindia.com/corporates/download/307881/IPO%20Prior/AITMCUpdatedDraftRedHerringProspectus30092026_20261006123402.pdf)

claims.claim: The company reports it established a collaboration with IIT Ropar in 2025 to indigenously develop entirely Indian drone technology, which includes building custom flight algorithms and AI-based guidance systems.
claims.source: IIT Ropar Centre of Drones and Autonomous Systems (https://iitrpr.ac.in/cdas/), Global Agriculture, Tribune India

claims.claim: The company's small class hexacopter agriculture spraying drone model, branded "VIRAJ", received Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) Type Certification in May 2024.
claims.source: ANI News (https://www.aninews.in/news/business/aitmc-ventures-ltd-avpl-international-bags-dgca-type-certification-for-agriculture-drone-viraj20240516163320), Business Standard, Bots & Drones India

claims.claim: The company inaugurated Phase-1 of its ₹80 crore "Drone City Haryana" in Sisai, Hansi, in May 2026, which features an 11.5-acre site with 23 industrial sheds dedicated to drone assembly and drone-component manufacturing.

AVPL International announced a strategic alliance with the Indian Farmers Fertilizer Cooperative Limited (IFFCO) in May 2024 to initiate drone spray operations across 20 lakh hectares (50 lakh acres) of farmland spanning eight Indian states.
claims.source: The Hindu BusinessLine (https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/agri-business/avpl-iffco-form-alliance-for-drone-spraying-in-8-states/article68199078.ece), The News Minute, Krishi Jagran

claims.claim: AVPL International signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with CSC e-Governance Services India Limited (CSC SPV) in November 2025 to distribute its "Viraj UAS" agricultural drones, spare parts, and training programs through a network of over 5 lakh village level entrepreneurs.
claims.source: Aviation World (https://aviationworld.in/avpl-international-and-csc-e-governance-services-signs-mou-for-drone-technology/), The Hindu BusinessLine, Electronics For You

claims.claim: The company's parent entity, AITMC Ventures Limited, reported an operating revenue of ₹41.87 crore for FY24, representing a 95.2% growth over the previous year, alongside profits of ₹8.84 crore.
claims.source: Polemarch Financials Profile (polemarch.in) & Planify FY24 Results Summary

claims.claim: For FY26, the parent entity reported a 26.3% increase in consolidated revenue to ₹106.8 crore, up from over ₹86.6 crore in FY25, while net profit held flat at ₹14.2 crore.
claims.source: The Foundation Nation Report on AITMC Ventures FY26 Financials & WWIPL Unlisted Shares Financial Report

claims.claim: IMK Capital invested in AVPL (AITMC Ventures) at an enterprise valuation of ₹500 crore in March 2023.
claims.source: ANI Press Release published via ThePrint & Business Standard (March 28, 2023)

claims.claim: Arbaaz Khan joined AVPL International as a strategic investor and brand ambassador in June 2025, contributing an undisclosed funding amount.
claims.source: Manifest Media, MediaNews4U and The Hindu Business Line corporate announcements (June 2025)

claims.claim: The company reports that its Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) network spans over 70 districts across 16 states and 3 Union Territories through strategic alliances with UPL, IFFCO, and DeHaat, supported by a network of over 75 training and service centers and 70 Centre of Excellences.
claims.note: The precise number of '70 Centre of Excellences' could not be confirmed in the published official materials.
claims.source: AVPL International Official Website (Drone-as-a-Service infrastructure documentation)

claims.claim: AVPL International has scaled its skilling infrastructure by establishing 30 Aero Vision Labs across 13 Indian states in collaboration with the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), alongside training facilities upgraded to Global Skills and Incubation Hubs across 12 states.
claims.note: training facilities upgraded to Global Skills and Incubation Hubs across 12 states

claims.claim: The company reports facilitating drone spraying across over 5 million acres (50 lakh acres) of farmland in eight Indian states through a major strategic alliance for drone spray operations with the Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative Limited (IFFCO).
claims.note: network of over 70 drone skill, training, and incubation centers that also serve as post-sales drone service centers

claims.claim: The company reports a geographic operational presence across more than 12 Indian states and has established a network of over 70 drone skill, training, and incubation centers that also serve as post-sales drone service centers.
claims.source: The Hindu Business Line, Manufacturing Today India, and ET Infra
